The driver's own written statement gives a safety reason for the message — "The rider tried to open the door while we were moving. I told her to sit down for her own safety." (F6) — which, if accepted, frames F4 as an instruction to prevent a door being opened on a moving vehicle on an expressway-speed trip (15.5 km, ~22 min, F1/F2), not as an intent to detain the rider.

The chat record is complete and internally consistent — 2 messages, every one timestamped (F5) — so the timing of F3 before F4 is fixed and cannot be disputed by either side; the reviewer should read the two messages in that one-minute sequence rather than as isolated phrases.

There is no routing or overcharge dimension that would independently justify a refund: actual distance was 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (-0.1 km, -0%) (F1) and duration 23.2 min against 22 min estimated (+1.4 min) (F2), so the fixed RydeX fare is not inflated by any deviation.

The complaint's "felt unsafe for the whole ride" is not a dangerous-driving or collision allegation and is unsupported by the only objective trip records, which show a near-optimal, normally-timed journey (F1, F2); a general feeling of unease should not by itself be escalated as a SAFE-2 accident/injury/dangerous-driving event.

The driver has 510 days on the platform, 786 trips in 90 days, a 4.66 rating and 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints in 90 days (F8), which is inconsistent with a pattern of intimidating riders and supports resolving this as an isolated, context-explained incident with no account action; the rider likewise has 0 disputes in 90 days (F7).

weaknesses: The strongest point for the rider is on the face of the record: F4 "Sit down or I lock the doors." is a conditional reference to locking the doors, and a tribunal may well read that as a threat of confinement — the driver's safety motive in F6 is a statement, and the same paragraph of the policy that hears the allegation (SAFE-1) gives the driver's post-trip explanation no privileged status.

The driver never sent any reassuring follow-up message after F4 — the sole rider message F3 ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here") is answered only by F4 and nothing else (F5), so the rider's claim that she was refused a stop has no contradicting message from my client.

There is no in-car audio, no stop fact and no GPS record of an actual door-open or of the doors being locked (the only gps facts are F1 and F2), so the safety justification in F6 rests on the driver's word alone and cannot be corroborated from the system records.

The rider's request to stop at 17:19 (F3) mid-trip is not addressed by any policy clause I can cite in the driver's favour; RD-3 covers agreed stops and pick-up waiting, not a rider's unilateral demand to be let out en route, so I cannot point to a clause excusing the refusal itself.

Nothing in my case prevents the reviewer from treating this as SAFE-1, in which case no refund formula applies at all and the outcome is entirely in the reviewer's hands (escalate), not a defended no_action.

events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.85)
events.body: This file is filed as a safety dispute and the screening clause SAFE-1 is engaged on its face: the rider asked to be let out ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3], 17:19) and the only reply in the record, one minute later, is the driver's "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4], 17:20. A conditional reference to locking the doors of a moving vehicle, sent in answer to a rider trying to exit, is capable of being read as a confinement threat; the completeness and timestamping of the record [F5] fixes that F3→F4 sequence and the driver cannot dispute F4 was sent as written. Per SAFE-1, therefore, no automatic ruling is made and the case goes to a human reviewer.

ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP human reviewer as a conduct/safety case (no fare remedy due): retrieve in-car audio or telematics (door-lock status, door-open warnings, vehicle speed at 17:19–17:21) for the window around F3/F4; obtain both parties' full statements; assess whether F4 constitutes a confinement threat under SAFE-1 or a reasonable safety instruction; if a confinement threat is found, apply code-of-conduct action; if the reviewer finds no conduct breach, no refund applies (fixed RydeX fare, actual 15.4 km vs optimal 15.5 km) and no account flag attaches (RD-6 not met: 0 upheld disputes in 90 d). Offer the rider the 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths if she reports distress.
ruling.reasoning: This file is filed as a safety dispute and the screening clause SAFE-1 is engaged on its face: the rider asked to be let out ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3], 17:19) and the only reply in the record, one minute later, is the driver's "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4], 17:20. A conditional reference to locking the doors of a moving vehicle, sent in answer to a rider trying to exit, is capable of being read as a confinement threat; the completeness and timestamping of the record [F5] fixes that F3→F4 sequence and the driver cannot dispute F4 was sent as written. Per SAFE-1, therefore, no automatic ruling is made and the case goes to a human reviewer.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's post-trip statement [F6] ('I told her to sit down for her own safety') is a statement, not consent or a clause-based justification, and RD-4 is a reroute exemption for road closures/incidents/severely slow traffic, which is not in issue here — there is no traffic fact and no off-route segment; the safety motive is for the human reviewer to weigh against the words actually sent under SAFE-1, not an automated defence.

Accepted only as to scope, and it does not help the driver: no collision, injury or dangerous-driving allegation is made, so SAFE-2 is not triggered; but that does not dispose of the conduct allegation, which routes to a human under SAFE-1 on F3/F4/F5.

Correct that RD-6's 'repeated' condition is not met (driver profile [F8]: 0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 d), so no flag_account attaches — but profile facts [F8] and the rider's profile [F7] cannot decide the case, and a clean profile does not answer the words in F4.

Accepted as to disposition (escalate) but the rider's report of feeling unsafe 'for the whole ride' is not corroborated beyond the one-minute exchange [F3][F4][F5]: the record documents 17:19–17:20 only, while the trip GPS [F1][F2] shows a near-optimal, normally-timed journey.
Accepted: profile facts [F8] cannot decide the case and RD-6 is not met, so no account-review referral for repeated misconduct arises from this record.

The only chat facts are F3 and F4 (both timestamped, record complete [F5]); the safety justification rests solely on the driver's post-trip statement [F6]. actions.detail: Safety dispute with a suspected SAFE-1 conduct issue (possible confinement threat at F4, in response to the rider's request to exit at F3), and the record lacks the audio/telematics needed to settle meaning or context; escalating for human review with no fare remedy (no off-route segment: 15.4 km actual vs 15.5 km optimal [F1]) and no account flag (RD-6 'repeated' condition not met on [F8]).

claims.assertion: The rider's own message at 17:19 asks the driver to stop and let her out (F3), and one minute later the driver replies with a threat to lock the doors (F4). That is a threat/intimidation by the driver against the rider.
The chat record contains both messages, each timestamped, so the threat in F4 is genuinely recorded and not an unverifiable statement (F5).

The driver's later written statement (F6) concedes there was a confrontation over the rider leaving the moving vehicle; his 'for her own safety' framing is his own after-the-fact characterisation of the words he actually sent in F4, and F4's words stand as written.

The rider reported feeling unsafe for the whole ride, and the driver's threat to lock her in is a confinement threat made while the trip was already 11 minutes underway; it is a safety incident, so no automatic ruling should be made and the case must go to a human reviewer.

The trip itself shows no routing or fare abuse (15.4 km actual vs 15.5 km optimal, F1; fixed $32.86 RydeX fare), so the only issue in this case is the safety conduct, reinforcing that the correct disposition is escalation rather than a fare ruling.

Driver profile: 510-day account, 4.66 rating, 786 trips, zero disputes in 90 days (F8) — the record shows no prior pattern, so this escalation is about the single incident and would support, at most, an account-review referral rather than a finding of repeated misconduct.

weaknesses: The complaint is based on a single 5-word driver message (F4) taken together with the rider's inability to dispute a driver's safety instruction; the driver will argue F6 that he was preventing the rider from opening a door on a moving car, and the GPS record (F1, F2) shows the ride was near-optimal and uneventful timing-wise, so there is no system record corroborating danger.

The rider's account says she felt unsafe 'for the whole ride', but the chat contains only chat #1 at 17:19 and chat #2 at 17:20 (F4, F5), so the record documents a one-minute exchange at 17:19–17:20, not continuous intimidation; the rider will need to explain the gap between what she reports and what the timestamped record shows.
No allegation of collision, injury or dangerous driving appears in the record (F1, F2, F3, F4, F6), so SAFE-2 is not established on the facts in this file; only SAFE-1 escalation can be argued.
Driver profile (F8) is clean and shows no prior upheld disputes, so any flag_account or pattern argument would be weakly supported; profile facts cannot decide the case anyway.

claims.assertion: The complaint alleges a threat of confinement ("threatened to lock me in"), and the chat does contain the driver's message "Sit down or I lock the doors." (F4) sent one minute after the rider's "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." (F3); a threat/intimidation allegation on the face of the record triggers screening, so this must go to a human reviewer rather than be decided by me or any automated ruling. I do not dispute that the message reads as a command and is capable of being read as a threat — my position is only that the context of it is safety, and that a person should decide.

The driver's own written statement gives a safety reason for the message — "The rider tried to open the door while we were moving. I told her to sit down for her own safety." (F6) — which, if accepted, frames F4 as an instruction to prevent a door being opened on a moving vehicle on an expressway-speed trip (15.5 km, ~22 min, F1/F2), not as an intent to detain the rider.

The chat record is complete and internally consistent — 2 messages, every one timestamped (F5) — so the timing of F3 before F4 is fixed and cannot be disputed by either side; the reviewer should read the two messages in that one-minute sequence rather than as isolated phrases.

There is no routing or overcharge dimension that would independently justify a refund: actual distance was 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (-0.1 km, -0%) (F1) and duration 23.2 min against 22 min estimated (+1.4 min) (F2), so the fixed RydeX fare is not inflated by any deviation.

The complaint's "felt unsafe for the whole ride" is not a dangerous-driving or collision allegation and is unsupported by the only objective trip records, which show a near-optimal, normally-timed journey (F1, F2); a general feeling of unease should not by itself be escalated as a SAFE-2 accident/injury/dangerous-driving event.

The driver has 510 days on the platform, 786 trips in 90 days, a 4.66 rating and 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints in 90 days (F8), which is inconsistent with a pattern of intimidating riders and supports resolving this as an isolated, context-explained incident with no account action; the rider likewise has 0 disputes in 90 days (F7).

weaknesses: The strongest point for the rider is on the face of the record: F4 "Sit down or I lock the doors." is a conditional reference to locking the doors, and a tribunal may well read that as a threat of confinement — the driver's safety motive in F6 is a statement, and the same paragraph of the policy that hears the allegation (SAFE-1) gives the driver's post-trip explanation no privileged status.

The driver never sent any reassuring follow-up message after F4 — the sole rider message F3 ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here") is answered only by F4 and nothing else (F5), so the rider's claim that she was refused a stop has no contradicting message from my client.

There is no in-car audio, no stop fact and no GPS record of an actual door-open or of the doors being locked (the only gps facts are F1 and F2), so the safety justification in F6 rests on the driver's word alone and cannot be corroborated from the system records.

The rider's request to stop at 17:19 (F3) mid-trip is not addressed by any policy clause I can cite in the driver's favour; RD-3 covers agreed stops and pick-up waiting, not a rider's unilateral demand to be let out en route, so I cannot point to a clause excusing the refusal itself.

Nothing in my case prevents the reviewer from treating this as SAFE-1, in which case no refund formula applies at all and the outcome is entirely in the reviewer's hands (escalate), not a defended no_action.

points.response: Agreed on the mechanism: F4 "Sit down or I lock the doors." sent one minute after the rider's F3 request to be let out is a threat/intimidation allegation for a person to read, so the rider does not seek an automated finding — but the same clause means the driver's context argument in F6 does not shrink the incident; the escalation stands.

F6 is the driver's post-trip statement, not a clause-based justification, and RD-4 (on which the driver relies) is a reroute/traffic exemption that has nothing to do with a spoken threat; a safety motive asserted only after the fact is exactly what SAFE-1 sends to a human to weigh against the words actually sent.

The sequence is agreed: F3 at 17:19 and F4 at 17:20, both timestamped and complete (F5) — and read in that sequence the record shows the rider asked to get out and the only reply she ever received was a conditional door-locking command, with no reassurance or explanation sent afterwards.

The rider does not seek any fare remedy — the trip was 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (F1) on a fixed $32.86 RydeX fare — so D4 is not in dispute and, by the driver's own admission, leaves the safety conduct in F4 as the sole live issue for the reviewer.

The rider relies on SAFE-1, not SAFE-2: the rider has not alleged a collision or dangerous driving on F1/F2, and her report of being threatened with being locked in (F3, F4, F6) is a conduct allegation that SAFE-1 routes to a human on its own terms.

The rider does not seek a flag_account or a pattern finding, so F7/F8 are irrelevant to the disposition; profile facts cannot decide the case (they are only ever supporting), and F8's clean record does not answer what was said in F4.

I do not contest that F3 (17:19, "Please stop the car, I want to get out here") is followed one minute later by F4 (17:20, "Sit down or I lock the doors."), and I accept that SAFE-1 screening is engaged by F4 on its face — my client's position is not that F4 is innocent on its words but that its context is the door-opening described in F6, and that a person must decide the meaning rather than an automated ruling.
Conceded insofar as F5 records 2 messages, every one timestamped, so the F3→F4 sequence is fixed and the driver cannot dispute that F4 was sent as written.

F6 is a post-trip statement and I do not claim it corroborates itself; but the rider's brief concedes the record shows no collision, injury or dangerous driving on the trip (F1 shows -0.1 km against the optimal route and F2 shows a normal 23.2 min), so there is no system record that proves the confrontation F6 describes either — the reviewer, not a rule, must weigh F4 against F6.

Agreed that the case routes to a human reviewer, so my client is not asking for an automatic no_action; but the rider's "unsafe for the whole ride" is contradicted by the only objective records, which show a near-optimal, normally-timed trip (F1, F2), and no in-car or door-lock record exists in the file, so the escalation should describe a one-minute exchange (F3, F4, F5) and not an unbroken course of intimidation.

I adopt this point: with actual distance 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (F1) and 23.2 min against 22 min estimated (F2), there is no deviated segment to compute anything under RD-2, and the fixed RydeX fare of $32.86 is not inflated — so the rider recovers no money on any fare theory and the file is a conduct question only.

I agree profile facts cannot decide the case (F8: 510-day account, 4.66 rating, 786 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days), and precisely because there is no prior upheld incident, RD-6's "repeated" condition is not met and no flag_account should attach to my client; the rider's own profile (F7: 0 disputes in 90 d) shows both parties are single-incident here.
